narrative.text: The first page of World Health Assembly resolution WHA71.7 on digital health (26 May 2018), which recalls earlier eHealth resolutions and recognizes the potential of digital technologies to support health systems and the Sustainable Development Goals. Its preamble stresses that digital solutions should complement existing services, that human interaction remains vital, and that technology transfer and cooperation matter.

Sets out what the resolution urges Member States to do, such as assess their use of digital technologies, integrate them into health systems and regulation, and build workforce digital skills. It also calls for public trust in digital health through work with civil society.

Continues the requests to Member States, including data protection legislation and partnerships across sectors. It then lists requests to the Director-General, starting with developing a global strategy on digital health and including guidance, a repository of evidence and collaboration with other UN bodies.
The final page of resolution WHA71.7, asking for a progress report to the Seventy-third World Health Assembly in 2020.
